extractor: read directly from the official GOV.UK pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state. The UK publishes no application form identifier for this route, so official_form_code is null everywhere and the online route is recorded as a step.
not_extracted: The table of eligible occupation codes, the going-rate salary table, the immigration salary list and the temporary shortage list. GOV.UK holds each in a separate document outside the registered sources, so VisaAI cannot yet tell an applicant whether their own occupation code qualifies or what their going rate is.

The sponsor licence fee (GBP 611 for small businesses and charities, GBP 1,682 for medium and large organisations). It is stated on the registered eligibility page but it is the EMPLOYER's fee, not the applicant's, so it is recorded in the description of the approved-employer condition rather than as a fee the applicant owes.
The lower salary rules for healthcare and education jobs based on national pay scales, and the full 'when you can be paid less' criteria — both on unregistered sub-pages.
Knowledge-of-English proof methods and accepted qualifications — unregistered sub-page /skilled-worker-visa/knowledge-of-english.
Dependant (partner and children) requirements and the money dependants must show — unregistered sub-page /skilled-worker-visa/your-partner-and-children.
The list of countries whose nationals must take a tuberculosis test, and the country-by-country criminal record certificate rules beyond the age/duration test quoted below.
Priority / faster-decision service fees — mentioned on the apply and landing pages with no amount stated.

requirements.label: Have a job offer from a UK employer approved by the Home Office
requirements.description: Approved employers are called sponsors. If your employer is not approved they can apply for a sponsor licence: GOV.UK states that costs the employer GBP 611 for small businesses and charities or GBP 1,682 for medium and large organisations, and takes around 8 weeks. That fee is the employer's, not the applicant's, so it is not listed as a fee here.
requirements.source_excerpt: you must have a job offer from an approved uk employer before you apply for a skilled worker visa. approved employers are also known as sponsors, because they are sponsoring you to come to or stay in the uk.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must have a job offer from an approved UK employer before you apply for a Skilled Worker visa. Approved employers are also known as sponsors, because they are sponsoring you to come to or stay in the UK.

requirements.label: Have a certificate of sponsorship (CoS) from your employer
requirements.description: The certificate of sponsorship is an electronic record, not a physical document. It carries a reference number you need for the visa application.

requirements.label: Do a job that is on the list of eligible occupations
requirements.description: Eligibility runs off a 4-digit occupation code. GOV.UK states a 'higher skilled' code qualifies outright; a 'medium skilled' code qualifies only if the job is on the immigration salary list, on the temporary shortage list, or is a prison officer (code 3314) extending or switching. Those lists are not registered sources, so VisaAI cannot yet resolve a specific code.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must meet all the following requirements to be eligible for a Skilled Worker visa: your job is eligible for this visa

requirements.label: Be paid at least the minimum salary for the type of work you will do
requirements.description: GOV.UK states GBP 41,700 per year or the going rate for the job, whichever is higher. Lower thresholds exist in stated cases: GBP 33,400 where you do not meet the usual requirement and do not work in healthcare or education, and GBP 31,300 for a prison officer extending or switching. The going-rate table is not a registered source.

parameters.comparator: highest of the standard minimum and the going rate for the occupation code

requirements.label: Have at least GBP 1,270 available to support yourself in the UK
requirements.description: GOV.UK requires the money to have been available for at least 28 days in a row, with day 28 falling within 31 days of applying. You do not usually need to show it if you have been in the UK on a valid visa for at least 12 months, or if your employer certifies on the certificate of sponsorship that it will cover your costs during your first month, up to GBP 1,270.
requirements.source_excerpt: you must have at least £1,270 in your bank account to show you can support yourself in the uk. you will need to have had the money available for at least 28 days in a row. day 28 must be within 31 days of applying for this visa.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must have at least £1,270 in your bank account to show you can support yourself in the UK. You will need to have had the money available for at least 28 days in a row. Day 28 must be within 31 days of applying for this visa.

requirements.label: Apply online for the Skilled Worker visa
requirements.description: The UK publishes no application form number for this route — the application exists only as an online service. GOV.UK states you can save the form and complete it later, and that you can apply up to 3 months before the start date listed on your certificate of sponsorship.
requirements.source_excerpt: you must apply online for a skilled worker visa.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You must apply online for a Skilled Worker visa.

requirements.label: Prove your identity, by app or at a visa application centre
requirements.description: GOV.UK states you will either use the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app to scan your identity document (creating or signing into a UKVI account), or have your fingerprints and photo taken at a visa application centre. You are told which when you apply. If you need an appointment you must take your passport, and the centre may be in another country.
requirements.source_excerpt: as part of your application, you’ll need to prove your identity. how you do this depends on where you’re from and what type of passport you have.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: As part of your application, you’ll need to prove your identity. How you do this depends on where you’re from and what type of passport you have.

requirements.label: Skilled Worker visa application fee
requirements.description: GOV.UK states the standard fee ranges from GBP 819 to GBP 1,865 depending on circumstances. From outside the UK: GBP 819 per person for up to 3 years, GBP 1,618 per person for more than 3 years. From inside the UK to extend, switch or update: GBP 943 for up to 3 years, GBP 1,865 for more than 3 years. If the job is on the immigration salary list the fee is GBP 628 for up to 3 years or GBP 1,235 for more than 3 years, the same inside or outside the UK. A partner or child joining you pays the fee for the same length of time as you.
